chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muyassar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man bought a skin sack of oil and found residue in it.' He said, 'If he knows that such residue is normally in the oil, he does not return it; and if he does not know that such residue is normally in the oil, he returns it to its owner.'

key_terms.دُرْدِيّاً: Residue, dregs, or sediment found at the bottom of a liquid.
key_terms.رَجُلٌ: A man (generic subject in legal examples).
key_terms.زِقَّ: A skin sack or bag used for storing liquids like oil or wine.
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: Its owner (referring to the seller in this context of return).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning a purchased item if it contains an unexpected residue?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'gharar' (uncertainty) in commercial transactions by distinguishing between customary residue and unexpected defects. It establishes that a buyer's right to return the item hinges on whether the impurity was known or expected at the time of purchase, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness and transparency in trade. The ruling underscores the importance of contextual knowledge in validating contractual consent.
